title: Optimal Approximate Quantum Conversion from a Taut-String Principle in Majorization-Based Resource Theories
authors: Franco Meroi, Cesar Massri, Marcelo Losada, Guido Bellomo, Gustavo Martin Bosyk
abstract: Optimal approximate state conversion is a fundamental task in quantum resource theories, yet existing solutions are largely tailored to specific distinguishability measures and resource theories. We show that every optimal approximate-conversion problem in the three paradigmatic majorization-based quantum resource theories of non-uniformity, bipartite pure-state entanglement, and pure-state coherence reduces exactly to one of only four elementary taut-string constructions. This holds for problems generated by Schur-convex spectral distances and by a broad family of quantum divergences satisfying a natural reduction property with respect to the corresponding equivalence group. The resulting framework encompasses a broad class of physically relevant distinguishability measures, including the trace distance, all unitarily invariant norms, quantum relative entropy, maximal quantum $f$-divergences, and the $α$-$z$ Rényi relative entropies. The increment vector of the corresponding taut string completely determines both the optimal approximation error and a canonical optimal state. Our results establish a common geometric framework for approximate quantum resource conversion, revealing that a broad class of seemingly different optimization problems is governed by the same taut-string geometric principle.
summary: This paper unifies the theory of approximate quantum resource conversion by showing that problems related to non-uniformity, entanglement, and coherence all reduce to solving a common geometric problem defined by the taut string. This framework provides a single mathematical tool to calculate optimal conversion errors and states across a wide range of physically relevant quantum measures.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental task of determining the optimal approximate state conversion between two quantum states when exact conversion is impossible within the context of Quantum Resource Theories.
main_result: It establishes that optimal approximate conversion problems across three major resource theories reduce exactly to one of only four elementary taut-string constructions, unifying the geometric framework for these problems.
method: The core method involves reducing complex quantum optimization problems involving quantum divergences or spectral distances to classical optimization problems over majorization polytopes, which are then solved using the taut-string construction.
model_or_system: The focus is on Majorization-Based Quantum Resource Theories (MQRTs), specifically those governing non-uniformity, bipartite pure-state entanglement, and pure-state coherence. The analysis uses state representations via probability vectors and associated majorization constraints.
key_observables: Optimal approximation error ($\epsilon_{\min}$), the optimal approximating state, and various quantum distinguishability measures (e.g., trace distance, quantum relative entropy).
important_parameters: The dimension of the state space ($n$), the support size of the target state ($m$), and the specific functional form of the quantum divergence ($f$-divergences, $\alpha$-Rényi).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that the quantum distinguishability measure reduces to a classical distinguishability measure depending only on the representative probability vectors, and that the problem can be mapped onto the geometry of the taut string.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the reduction to a taut-string construction constrained by majorization floor/roof. Figure 2 classifies the problems using the four elementary taut-string geometries (T1-T4).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the reduction of three distinct quantum resource theories (non-uniformity, entanglement, coherence) to a common mathematical structure—the taut string—by solving the minimization problem for various quantum divergences.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, unifying mathematical tool (the taut string) to analyze resource conversion problems in quantum information, suggesting a deep geometric principle underlying seemingly disparate physical constraints.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of optimal approximate conversion in MQRTs. The initial state (ρ) cannot be converted exactly into the target (σ) because it lies outside the reachable set under the resource preorder, represented here by the batter- ies. The best admissible approximation (τ) is then selected by minimizing the chosen error measure d, encoded by the color gradient. In MQRTs, this problem is solved exactly by a taut- string construction constrained by the majorization floor (Fk) and roof (Gk). The construction for approximations over the upper conversion set is entirely analogous.

FIG. 1. Taut strings T1 and T2 for the pair (⃗x, ⃗y) of Sec. VIII. They solve the lower- and upper-majorization-polytope problems, respectively, for the Schur-convex objectives g(⃗y −⃗x ′). Dashed lines denote the floor and roof, with the boundary shared by T1 and T2 shown in black; solid lines denote the corresponding taut strings.

FIG. 2. Taut strings T3 and T4 for the same pair (⃗x, ⃗y). They solve the lower- and upper-majorization-polytope f-divergence problems, respectively, and, through the fidelity reduction, the corresponding pure-state entanglement and coherence problems.
